name: m4-threads
description: Interner tables under G1: does keeping the table out of humongous regions (no old-to-young stores per insert, no card scanning) make a compile-shaped workload faster? One op is one simulated compile (5M lookups, ~3.7 GB allocated, ~200 MB live), compiles back to back, G1, 8 GB heap, Graal 25.4.4.

Concurrency: 1, 2 or 4 compiles at once in one JVM (one table each). Hypothesis: with chained tables the time per compile grows faster with concurrency, since each humongous table adds card scanning to every young pause that all threads wait on.

variantDescriptions.cw-t1: 1 concurrent compiles, each with its own `chained-weak` table
variantDescriptions.cw-t2: 2 concurrent compiles, each with its own `chained-weak` table
variantDescriptions.cw-t4: 4 concurrent compiles, each with its own `chained-weak` table
variantDescriptions.kw-t1: 1 concurrent compiles, each with its own `chunked-weak` table
variantDescriptions.kw-t2: 2 concurrent compiles, each with its own `chunked-weak` table
variantDescriptions.kw-t4: 4 concurrent compiles, each with its own `chunked-weak` table
